name: The Mughal Age: Domes, Dynasties and the Company
description: From Babur's victory at Panipat in 1526 to the end of the dynasty in 1858: the emperors, their cities and the Taj Mahal, their Maratha rivals, and the trading company that took their place.

checkpoints.name: Babur and Panipat
checkpoints.note: Babur, a Timurid prince driven from Central Asia, took Kabul and in 1526 beat the sultan of Delhi at the First Battle of Panipat with cannon and muskets, founding the Mughal Empire. To the west Safavid Iran rose as a rival and a model, and Sikhism grew in Punjab.

checkpoints.name: The empire of Akbar
checkpoints.note: Akbar became emperor in 1556, enlarged the empire across the north, built the city of Fatehpur Sikri and made Persian the language of government. Hampi, the capital of the southern kingdom, was sacked in 1565, the Sikhs' Golden Temple at Amritsar was begun, and in 1600 the English East India Company was founded.

checkpoints.name: The age of the Taj
checkpoints.note: Shah Jahan ruled in the empire's richest days and built the Taj Mahal for his wife and a new capital at Delhi. The Dutch East India Company and the English at Bombay traded on the coasts. Aurangzeb took the throne in 1658 and pushed the empire to its widest, but his long wars against Shivaji's Marathas drained it.

checkpoints.name: Marathas and invaders
checkpoints.note: After Aurangzeb's death in 1707 the emperors lost real power. The Maratha Empire spread across the centre and west of India, a Persian army sacked Delhi in 1739, and the European companies fortified their trading towns.

checkpoints.name: The Company takes control
checkpoints.note: After the Battle of Plassey in 1757 the East India Company became a ruling power, known as Company rule in India. In 1857 the Indian Rebellion rallied around the last Mughal emperor in Delhi; after it was crushed the British exiled him, ended the Mughal Empire and in 1858 took India from the Company.
